body.summary: Fresh-context audit of P30-I20-W58 (commit d0ef1bb1) against its 2 criteria. Both hold. CR-01 (open watch tail picks up newly-persisted chunks each poll tick): the fix hoists _sync_output_from_store (agent_watch.py:1945) into the state-reactive poll-backstop watcher _on_app_state (agent_watch.py:2019), registered at :1891, calling it UNCONDITIONALLY before the parity early-exit at :2021 -- pre-W58 the tail only backfilled on mount and same-fleet poll ticks hit the early-exit. Sync reads persisted agent.output.chunk lines off the event store, independent of live daemon push. Test test_agent_watch_tail_syncs_new_chunks_from_store_on_poll (test_modes_agent_watch.py:562) passes. CR-02 (store sync + live push never double-render): per-recompose count cursor (agent_watch.py:1775 reset; :1985-1987 advance) plus OutputTail.replace clearing all prior rows incl live-push (output_tail.py:257) on first content sync, plus append_output gated off once store owns the tail (:2129-2130). All 3 refutation orderings (push-then-sync, sync-then-push, cap-shift edge) fail to produce a duplicate. Tests test_output_tail_replace_clears_prior_rows_and_reseeds + poll test (asserts count==1) pass. Verdict pass-with-followups because refutation surfaced one genuine latent defect not covered by either criterion for bounded output.

followups.title: 500-line cap-shift freezes long-spawn watch tails
followups.detail: Count-based cursor (agent_watch.py:1985-1987, len(lines)>cursor) vs the shifting lines[-500:] window (agent_watch.py:722, _OUTPUT_BACKFILL_LIMIT=500) means once a spawn exceeds 500 output lines len(lines) plateaus at 500 while the window shifts forward, so the tail freezes at the first 500-line window and drops later chunks. Use a content/seq identity anchor instead of len().

followups.title: CR-01 has no test through the real _on_app_state poll path
followups.detail: Sole test calls _sync_output_from_store() directly (test_modes_agent_watch.py:591) so the poll-tick wiring at agent_watch.py:2019 is verified by reading, not by a test. Add a test that advances state.json mtime to drive _on_app_state end-to-end.

body.summary: The D-LOCK-SPLIT restructure meets all three declared success criteria: the deterministic oracle tier + floor pack + rollup reads run before portalock.acquire, the under-lock section is reduced to re-read/version-recheck/verdict-tier/apply/validate/WAL/fsync/event-append, the optimistic re-check refuses a close only when the TARGET wave row changed (unrelated rows tolerated) with a typed close_preflight_stale error, and a concurrent mutate lands inside its 5s window while the close sits off-lock. The four new tests in tests/daemon/test_close_lock_split.py pass and independently exercise CR-01/CR-02/CR-03. One collateral regression: the wave relocated the run_close_preflight call from mutate() into the new _mutate_wave_close() without updating tests/workflow/verify/test_preflight.py::test_daemon_close_pipeline_calls_run_close_preflight, which asserts `await run_close_preflight(` and the injected seams live in inspect.getsource(daemon_state.mutate); that test passed before the wave and now fails, so the committed suite is red until it is repointed at _mutate_wave_close. Functional deliverable is correct; the stale introspection test is a required follow-up before iter/phase close.

criteria.criterion: Floor pack and deterministic oracle tier execute BEFORE portalock.acquire; under-lock reduced to re-read + re-check + jury tier + apply + validate + WAL + fsync + event append
Optimistic re-check refuses a close when a concurrent writer mutated the target wave row between pre-flight and lock, and re-runs pre-flight only when the wave row itself changed
A concurrent state.mutate RPC completes within its 5s acquire window while a close with a long deterministic gate is in the off-lock pre-flight phase

refutations: tests/workflow/verify/test_preflight.py::test_daemon_close_pipeline_calls_run_close_preflight now FAILS (verified: 1 failed, 88 passed): it asserts `await run_close_preflight(` and the three injected seams appear in inspect.getsource(daemon_state.mutate), but W09 moved that call into the new _mutate_wave_close(), so the source-introspection assertion at line 138 breaks. The test passed on the parent commit, making this a wave-introduced suite regression the full-tree iter-close gauntlet will catch; it must be repointed at _mutate_wave_close before the iter/phase closes.
